Subjective:
- Presenting complaints (3-week history):
  • Reduced hearing on left side.  
  • Numbness of left face around ear and jawline, constant.  
  • Occasional ringing (tinnitus) in left ear, sometimes accompanied by mild dizziness.  
- Denies: limb weakness or numbness, dysphagia, dysarthria, visual changes, ear discharge, ear pain, fever, pruritus in ear.  
- Past medical history: nasal polyps; prior episode of labyrinthitis (remote, resolved).  
- Medications: intranasal spray for nasal polyps (name/dose/route/frequency not documented, used PRN); Rennie antacid tablets PRN.  
- Social history: professional jockey; reduced training due to symptoms; lives with partner; no pets.  
- Family history: brother with neurofibromatosis.  
- Allergies: latex.  

Objective:
(No physical examination performed during video consultation.)  
- Planned exam: full cranial nerve and neurological examination, otoscopic exam.  
- Investigations: none completed at time of call.  

Assessment & Plan:

1. Left-sided facial numbness, hypoacusis, tinnitus  
   - Assessment: Suspected Bell’s palsy.  
   - Differential diagnosis: otologic infection, labyrinthitis recurrence, acoustic neuroma, cerebrovascular event.  
   - Investigations planned: same-day face-to-face clinic visit for detailed neurological and otoscopic examination; further imaging or audiology testing if indicated after exam.  
   - Treatment planned: contingent on in-person findings (e.g., oral corticosteroids/antivirals if Bell’s palsy confirmed).  
   - Referrals: none yet; will consider ENT or neurology referral after examination.

2. Health-related anxiety about seriousness of symptoms  
   - Assessment: situational anxiety secondary to above symptoms.  
   - Treatment planned: Reassurance provided; further reassurance to be offered after physical examination results.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected: vitals, cranial nerve exam findings, medication name/dosage for nasal spray, comprehensive medication list verification.  
● No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
● Transcript quality: clear; minor conversational pauses but clinically adequate.
